anomalies.observed: Q1's gate is connected to Q2's collector and one side of C3; the other side of C3 connects to VCC. There is no DC pull-up from the gate to the PMOS source.
anomalies.expected: A PMOS gate driven low by Q2 should have a DC pull-up to its source (VCC) so Q1 turns off when Q2 is off.
anomalies.impact: When Q2 pulls Q1's gate low, C3 can hold the gate near that voltage after Q2 turns off. Q1 may remain on or behave unpredictably instead of reliably switching the fan supply off.

anomalies.observed: Both the ATtiny45 (U2) and ATtiny13 (U3) are connected in parallel on their corresponding supply, reset, and I/O pins, including their PWM outputs.
anomalies.expected: The board should use one controller, or provide isolation/selection so two populated MCUs do not drive the same nets.

anomalies.impact: If both listed MCUs are populated, they can contend on shared outputs and may execute different firmware, making controller operation unreliable or causing electrical stress.
